sentences.text: Following a storm-related recovery, control of coagulation and filtration returns to normal only after raw-water quality trends support stable chemical feed and predictable filter loading.
The Chief Operator establishes the starting coagulant dose from recent turbidity, color, alkalinity, pH, temperature, and bench-scale treatment observations.
The Coagulant Dosing Skid, known locally as Marigold, meters the primary coagulant under automatic control during routine operation.
The Coagulant Dosing Skid sends the Alum Batch Ticket when a new chemical lot is placed into service.
Automatic dose trimming is based on analyzer feedback, operator-entered targets, and verified process response rather than on a single instrument value.
When raw-water turbidity changes quickly, the Duty Engineer may authorize a temporary dose adjustment while the Chief Operator confirms the sustained control point.
The North Filter Gallery, known locally as Cobalt, contains a bank of gravity filters operated from the plant control system.
North Filter Gallery records individual filter effluent turbidity and headloss at the end of each control scan.
South Filter Gallery sends the Filter Run Exception Note when a filter run ends outside the normal operating limits.
Filter run management is based on run time, terminal headloss, effluent turbidity, prior backwash quality, and the current condition of upstream treatment.
A filter is not returned to service after washing until rinse-to-waste quality meets the operating target and the turbidity trend is stable.
If a filter shows an unusual turbidity rise, operating staff compare the analyzer trend with nearby sample results before declaring a process upset.
The Laboratory Technician provides confirmation testing when online analyzers disagree with observed filter performance or with routine process samples.
The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is used for custody-controlled receipt of compliance and process samples collected from treatment locations.
The SCADA Historian Server retains dose changes, analyzer values, filter status changes, wash sequences, and operator comments for later review.
Manual override is permitted for chemical feed, valve sequencing, and filter start or stop actions only when automatic control is unavailable or inappropriate for the condition.
An operator placing equipment in manual control is expected to state the reason, monitor the affected process variable closely, and restore automatic control as soon as practicable.
Manual chemical feed changes are made in small increments unless an immediate water-quality risk requires a larger correction approved by the Chief Operator.
If analyzer feedback is lost, operating staff hold the last verified safe dose or revert to an approved fixed dose while collecting additional grab samples.
A sustained loss of coagulation effectiveness is treated as a process deviation and prompts review of chemical strength, feed pump status, mixing energy, and raw-water characteristics.
The Chlorine Contact Basin is considered in the response because excessive particulate carryover can affect downstream disinfectant demand and contact performance.
The Clearwell Level Controller remains coordinated with filter production so that filter shutdowns, backwashes, and return-to-service decisions do not create avoidable storage swings.
When filter capacity is reduced, the Distribution Dispatcher is advised of expected production limits before changes affect the High Service Pump Header.
After any significant deviation, the Chief Operator reviews trends from the affected operating period and confirms that corrective actions restored stable clarified and filtered water quality.
